tareas.explicacion: Automatic work runs apart from the screens and with lower priority: if it gets stuck or crashes, the screens keep working and it restarts by itself. For now it does the system's work: every hour it checks the queue and whether there was an update, every night it checks and tidies the database, and at 4:40 a.m. it makes the locked backup, sends it to your Telegram and checks it. Your projects start using it with the customer search (phase 2).

ia.que_es: What it does and what it costs
ia.que_es.texto: For now it only helps understand a project's instructions, if you turned on “Help in projects”, when someone asks and accepts the price (about US$0.0005 each time). Projects will be able to use it in their automatic work from phase 2, and only if you allow it in an approved version.
ia.mes.titulo: When does the AI month start?
ia.mes.texto: It is the same month the provider bills by: it starts on day 1 at midnight universal time. In the Dominican Republic that is 8:00 p.m. on the last day of the previous month.
ia.ayuda.texto: Lets you ask AI for help on a version waiting for approval (a new project or a change). Each time you see the price and confirm.
ia.ayuda.confirmar: Turn on AI help in projects? It works on any version waiting for approval: a new project or a change to one that already runs. It does not use each project's AI permission (that permission is for the automatic work, which comes later), so it does not wait for your permission in each project: every time someone asks they see the price and must confirm, always within the cap. You approve the version AI makes.
ia.solo_dueno: To change anything, open OPORTIA from your iPhone or Mac with your Tailscale account, through the https link.
ia.solo_el_dueno: Only the owner of OPORTIA (the first administrator account) changes the AI and the keys. From your account you can see the spending and turn the AI off.

ia.pago.claude: Claude is billed separately, in the Claude Console (console.anthropic.com → Billing), with credit you buy in advance. It is not your Claude chat subscription or balance.
ia.pago.limite: Create an “oportia” workspace there (Workspaces), make the key inside it and give it a spend limit a little above this cap (the cap + 20%, at least US$1 more). Keep auto-reload off.
ia.pago.limite.por_que: If the limit were equal to the cap, the provider could stop OPORTIA too early. The “Default” workspace cannot have a limit.
ia.pago.openai: ChatGPT (OpenAI) is also billed separately, at platform.openai.com → Billing; it is not your ChatGPT subscription.

copias.restaurar.titulo: If you ever lose the server
copias.restaurar.paso1: Have your recovery key at hand (the one on paper or in Passwords).
copias.restaurar.paso2: In Telegram open @BotFather → /mybots → your bot → API Token, and copy it.
copias.restaurar.paso3: On the new server, OPORTIA will ask for that token and your key. It finds your latest backup by itself (the one pinned at the top of the chat with your bot), checks it and opens it.
copias.restaurar.paso4: Right away, revoke the bot token: in @BotFather type /revoke, choose your bot and it gives you a NEW token. That way the old server, if it is still alive, can no longer send its old backups to your chat.
copias.restaurar.paso5: Then paste your AI keys and the NEW bot token again in Keys (for safety they never travel in the backups). Next, create a new recovery key in Backups and keep both: the old one opens the old backups.
copias.restaurar.paso6: Do not delete the bot's messages: they are your backups. If you delete the chat, only the backups on this server remain.
copias.restaurar.nota: The restore screen arrives in part 1f; until then, Claude does it with you through the server console, with the same steps.
copias.clave.no_puede.solo_desde_tailnet: The key is created and checked from your Tailscale account, not through the public link.
copias.clave.no_puede.solo_dueno_tailsca: The key is created and checked with your Tailscale account, through the https link.
copias.clave.no_puede.solo_el_dueno: Only the owner of OPORTIA creates and checks the key, from their Tailscale account.

copias.clave.comprobar_ayuda: Type it looking at your paper or your Passwords. That way you know it is stored well. The key does not leave this screen.
copias.clave.actual: It is your key {huella}: it opens your backups since {desde} (the latest: {mb}, {tablas} tables).

ayuda.linea: Search for a word and read what it means.
ayuda.buscar.vacio: No word matches “{texto}”. Try a shorter one.
ayuda.proyecto.texto: A project is a job you give OPORTIA: which customers or which job you are looking for, and where. You create it by tapping options, OPORTIA shows you what it understood, and you approve it.
ayuda.proyecto.ejemplo: “I sell solar panels to hotels in Punta Cana.”
ayuda.entendi.texto: It is the summary OPORTIA builds from what you asked: who to look for, where and how. Read it before approving; if something is off, you fix it right there.
ayuda.aprobar.texto: Approving is giving your OK to what OPORTIA understood: nothing is used without your approval. For now, approving leaves the project saved and ready; it does not search yet (that comes in phase 2).
ayuda.trabajo_automatico.texto: It is the part of OPORTIA that works on its own 24 hours a day, even when you close the screen. Today it looks after the server and makes the backups; when search arrives, it will also do the work of your projects.
ayuda.modo_seguro.texto: It is a pause of all automatic work. It turns on by itself if something fails several times in a row, or you turn it on. The screens keep working and nothing is lost: when you turn it off, work continues where it stopped.
ayuda.modo_seguro.ejemplo: If automatic work crashes 5 times in 15 minutes, OPORTIA enters safe mode by itself and tells you.
ayuda.aviso.texto: A notice tells you something needs your attention: yellow means “look when you can” and red means “look now”. “Got it” marks it as seen; the notice goes away by itself when the problem is fixed.
ayuda.servidor.texto: It is the always-on computer where OPORTIA lives and your data is stored. Green: all good. Yellow: worth a look. Red: something needs fixing.
ayuda.copia.texto: It is a duplicate of all your data, locked. It is made automatically every night and leaves the server for your Telegram, so you lose nothing if the server breaks.
ayuda.copia_comprobada.texto: A backup is checked when OPORTIA downloaded it back from Telegram and confirmed it is complete and can be opened. Only those count as good backups.
ayuda.copia_comprobada.ejemplo: “Backups: today 4:41 AM” in green means last night’s backup is checked.
ayuda.clave_recuperacion.texto: It is a long key (7 groups of letters and numbers) that only you have: OPORTIA shows it when you create it and does not keep it. It opens your backups if you ever lose the server; without it, nobody can open them, not even you.
ayuda.clave_recuperacion.ejemplo: Write it on paper or save it in your iPhone Passwords, never on the server itself.
ayuda.telegram.texto: It is the messaging app where OPORTIA sends you backups and serious notices. You create a bot (a free automatic contact) and link it to your chat; you do it once, in Keys.
ayuda.token.texto: It has two uses. In Telegram, the token is your bot’s key: @BotFather gives it to you and you paste it once. In AI, a token is a small piece of a word, and the price is charged per million tokens.
ayuda.token.ejemplo: “Hello, how are you?” is fewer than 10 tokens.
ayuda.ia.texto: It is optional help that costs money: it understands better what you write in your own words. It starts turned off, and OPORTIA works fully without it, with its own free engine.
ayuda.tope.texto: It is the most AI can spend in a month. You set it, in dollars, and OPORTIA never goes over it: when the cap is reached, AI stops until the next month.
ayuda.tope.ejemplo: With a US$5 cap, AI stops by itself on reaching US$5.
ayuda.clave_api.texto: They are the permissions that let OPORTIA use outside services, such as Telegram or Claude. You paste them once, they are stored encrypted and only their last 4 characters are shown. They are not your sign-in password.
ayuda.plan.texto: An account’s plan says how many projects it can have in use at once: Trial 1, Paid 5 and Business 20. The administrator changes it. Projects in the trash do not count.
ayuda.clave_temporal.texto: It is the password the administrator gives a person to sign in the first time (or if they forgot theirs). On signing in, OPORTIA asks them to change it for their own.
ayuda.clave_temporal.ejemplo: Read it to them over the phone: it stops being shown when you leave Administrator.
ayuda.tailscale.texto: It is the private network that connects your devices (your iPhone and your PC) to the server. The most sensitive things, such as keys, the recovery key or creating accounts, can only be done through it, not through the public link.
